question: Which upgrade cuts the time between frames more: 30 to 60 Hz, or 60 to 360 Hz?
answer: 30 to 60 Hz. Frame time is one second divided by the rate: 30 Hz gives 33.3 ms and 60 Hz gives 16.7, a saving of 16.7 ms. Going from 60 to 360 Hz takes 16.7 ms down to 2.8, saving 13.9. Each doubling saves half what the last one did.
move: When a rate rises, compare the time it saves, not the rates.
trap: A sixfold jump in rate looks bigger than a mere doubling.
reference: Larrick & Soll, The MPG Illusion, Science 320, 2008
